notes: §1985:XV.3.2.4 GR1: "Automatic execution of a debugging section is not caused by a statement appearing in a debugging section." StatementBinder.Bind sets _inDebuggingSection from ProcedureTableBuilder.IsDebuggingSection so BindStatement plans no data, file or cd fire for such a statement, and EmitterState.DebugCauseAssignments records __dbgInSection at each transfer (and __dbgRaisedInSection for a raised USE procedure) which EmitDebugRunner and EmitRunUseBody read; the witness PERFORMs a monitored procedure and MOVEs to a monitored item from the section. Probes at 85 (work-rr-09/dbg/g1a, g1b): from one debugging section a MOVE to another section's data-name, a DISPLAY of an ALL REFERENCES item, a subscripted store, OPEN/WRITE/CLOSE/READ of a monitored file, a GO TO a monitored paragraph and an OPEN failure raising a USE procedure monitored by a third section ran none, while the same statements in MAIN ran each; ALL PROCEDURES skipped the debugging section's own paragraphs (PERFORM inside it). At --std 2002 USE FOR DEBUGGING is refused (COBOL0902). Side observations, other rules: a PERFORM of a nondeclarative paragraph from a debugging section draws only warning COBOL2375 (SR2), and a USE FOR DEBUGGING naming a debugging-section paragraph compiles (SR5, kb/Work PB5081).

next.reason: 1985: "Automatic execution of a debugging section is not caused by a statement appearing in a debugging section."; 2023: "No USE FOR DEBUGGING: the 2023 USE rules cover only exception, EC-I-O and BEFORE REPORTING declaratives". No 2023 clause holds the Debug feature. The USE candidates treat exception, I-O and report declaratives only, so debugging sections and this rule are gone.
